backend.database.core.funcs

Service-layer operations for authentication, conversations, and messages.

All functions are wrapped with the @transactional decorator, which manages SQLAlchemy sessions and transactions automatically. Each function accepts (and uses) an injected session: Session provided by the decorator.

This module provides high-level operations that orchestrate DAO calls and auxiliary services (encryption, email).

Module Contents

login_user(session: sqlalchemy.orm.Session, username: str, password: str) → backend.api.models.UserAuthentication[source]

Authenticate a user by username and password.

Parameters:

  • session (Session) -- Active SQLAlchemy session (injected by @transactional).

  • username (str) -- Username to authenticate.

  • password (str) -- Plaintext password to verify.

Returns:

A dict-like structure with:

  • authenticated (bool): True if credentials are valid.

  • detail (str): Error or info message.

  • user_details (dict | None): On success: {username, email, verified}; on failure may contain partial info.

Return type:

UserAuthentication

Notes

  • Uses EncryptionDec.check_passwords for constant-time verification.

  • If the username does not exist, returns authenticated=False with a message.

check_create_user_instance(session: sqlalchemy.orm.Session, username: str, password: str, email: str)[source]

Validate uniqueness, validate password policy, create a new user, and send a verification code.

Parameters:

  • session (Session) -- Active SQLAlchemy session (injected by @transactional).

  • username (str) -- Desired username (must be unique).

  • password (str) -- Plaintext password to be validated and hashed at DAO level.

  • email (str) -- Email address (must be unique).

Returns:

  • On success: {'res': True, 'detail': <verification_code>}

  • On failure: {'res': False, 'detail': <reason>}

Return type:

dict

Notes

  • Checks for existing username and email.

  • Validates password via EncryptionDec.is_valid_password.

  • Creates User with a generated verification code.

  • Sends the verification code via email.

send_verification_code(email: str, code: str) → None[source]

Send a verification code to the given email using Gmail SMTP.

Parameters:

  • email (str) -- Recipient email address.

  • code (str) -- Verification code to send.

Notes

  • Uses settings.SENDER_EMAIL and settings.APP_PASSWORD for SMTP auth.

  • Sends plain-text email via smtp.gmail.com:587 with STARTTLS.

  • Exceptions are propagated to the caller.

check_verification_code(session: sqlalchemy.orm.Session, username: str, user_code: str)[source]

Verify a user's email by checking their verification code and its expiry.

Parameters:

  • session (Session) -- Active SQLAlchemy session (injected by @transactional).

  • username (str) -- Username whose code is being verified.

  • user_code (str) -- Code provided by the user.

Returns:

  • {'res': True, 'detail': ''} if verified.

  • {'res': False, 'detail': <reason>} if expired or mismatch.

Return type:

dict

Notes

  • Code expires in 2 minutes from user.code_created_on.

resend_ver_code(session: sqlalchemy.orm.Session, username: str, email: str) → None[source]

Generate and send a new verification code for a user.

Parameters:

  • session (Session) -- Active SQLAlchemy session (injected by @transactional).

Raises:

Exception -- Propagates any errors from DAO update or SMTP send.

create_message(session: sqlalchemy.orm.Session, conversation_id: str, text: str, role: str, id: str, feedback: bool | None = None)[source]

Create a new message within a conversation and update the conversation's last_updated timestamp.

Returns:

{'id': <UUID>, 'message': <str>, 'timestamp': <datetime>, 'role': <str>}

Return type:

dict
